summary.intent: Orchestrate multiple waves of parallel-agent development on the CipherBox v2 rewrite: issue hygiene and dependency-graph maintenance, planning and executing waves 6-9 of implementation PRs, running CodeRabbit review cycles under a one-review-per-hour ceiling, and ultimately driving toward a demonstrable end-to-end vertical slice (login → create a file → reload → still there).
summary.outcome: Landed dozens of PRs across multiple waves (rotation/grant security fixes, prune/retire-ledger, owner-local sealed storage, first-run vault provisioning, ManualRefresh, web-e2e write-path coverage, worker validation), fixed several critical security defects found via mandatory review gates, filed ~60 well-hygiened tracker issues and 3 ADRs, built and repeatedly hardened a bash-based CodeRabbit review-cycle automation, and diagnosed a major architectural regression (v2 dropped CipherBox-as-identity-provider vs v1) culminating in a drafted ADR 0008 to restore wallet/email as first-class web logins.

repo: This repo squash-merges everything, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and `git branch -d` always report merged branches as unmerged — must gate on GitHub PR state via `gh` instead, and delete with `-D`.

CodeRabbit's clean verdict is a review submission on the head commit with a ZERO-LENGTH body, not a status-comment string; nitpicks live only in a `🧹 Nitpick comments (N)` collapsible in the review body with NO inline threads, invisible to `reviewThreads` GraphQL queries.
A running GitHub check-run has `conclusion: ""` (empty string), not null — `select(.conclusion==null)` for 'pending' silently never matches running checks.
Bash tool commands run under zsh, not bash: `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is empty (use `$pipestatus`), and unquoted `$VAR` expansions don't word-split, breaking `env -u X cmd --flag` patterns.

GitHub review comment `commit_id` is re-anchored to the current head when the file/line survive, so `commit_id==$head` can report old findings as new; use `original_commit_id` or fence on `created_at`.
Any new commit pushed to an already-ready (non-draft) PR triggers a CodeRabbit incremental review and spends the hourly slot — not just the ready-flip itself.
GitHub issue dependency edges are removed from the BLOCKED side (`/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by/{id}`), not the blocking side — DELETE on the wrong endpoint fails silently.
`pnpm lint:tracker-refs` only matches bare `#\d{3,5}` and never inspects prose like 'ADR 0005', so citing it as evidence a doc claim is 'safe' is vacuous.
Kubo's gateway 301-redirects a `localhost` Host path request to `<cid>.ipfs.localhost`, which resolves nowhere in a browser — must use `127.0.0.1:8080` for `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL`.

`docker/docker-compose.yml`'s `mock-ipns-routing` image is stale/broken (Dockerfile runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` against an npm lockfile); working local recipe is `cd tools/mock-ipns-routing && npm ci && npm run build && node dist/index.js`.

v1 (previous version) implemented wallet/passwordless-email login by having CipherBox's own API act as identity provider (`loginWithJWT` via a custom Web3Auth verifier); v2 switched to Web3Auth's own hosted OAuth (`loginWithOAuth`), which structurally cannot support wallet-as-first-login or CipherBox-owned passwordless email — this was an undocumented architectural regression, not a deliberate tradeoff.

`apps/desktop` is a 43-line static HTML stub with zero JS/bundler/dependencies and no engine binding (`main.rs` says 'Scaffold only'); `packages/client` is web-only by blueprint design and cannot be the vehicle for desktop-shared code.

AGENTS.md exempts frozen decision-corpus citations (bare `#NN D#` or `FSM1/cipher-box-next#NN`) from the no-tracker-refs-in-code rule, but bare `#NN` inside `cipher-box` (not cipher-box-next) autolinks to the wrong repo's issue since cipher-box's counter is past 1000.

code.finding: rejection_verdict exhaustively maps RejectionReason to Option<RefreshVerdict>; EpochBelowFloor deliberately maps to None (not Rejected) because it's sweep-pending staleness that no retry of the pass can clear — folding it into Unreachable/RefreshFailed would advertise a retry that provably cannot work, contradicting SweepResolveFailure::Superseded's existing is_retryable()=false precedent.

require_vacant_vault_pointer implements a positive-evidence-only vacancy probe (recovery cache 404 + every routing endpoint individually answering 'no record') to prevent inferring 'new account' from a total-outage false negative, which would silently mint a second genesis vault over an existing one and destroy the only copy of a non-re-derivable write scope seed.

seal_owner_local doc corrected to state ephemeral reuse is a break only 'under one recipient key AND info' (not just one recipient key), matching suite/hpke.rs:74's actual scoping — a looser doc would have condemned a legitimate cross-family KAT vector using a shared ephemeral with different info strings.

acquire() sets waiter.read=true, and fail()→drop()→settleIdle() resolves with that already-true flag, so a mid-read broker failure makes whenStreamIdle resolve true — causing useFileDownload.save (pre-fix) to report a truncated/failed download as success.

KUBO_API_URL is read only here in the entire codebase; unset it, pin() throws ServiceUnavailableException (uploads 503) while unpin() silently no-ops — staging's deploy-staging.yml set dead v1-era variable names (IPFS_PROVIDER, DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL etc.) instead.

workflow: Delegate CodeRabbit review-finding resolution to a sub-agent via /resolve-pr-reviews rather than triaging findings inline in the main orchestrator loop — the user corrected this multiple times.

Never apply a CodeRabbit-suggested fix literally without verifying its stated mechanism against the actual code; across the session at least 7 distinct cases where the literal suggestion would have been worse than the original bug (e.g. legacy-slot fallback for a population that can't exist, weakening a security check, breaking a passing test).

Batch multiple loosely-related issues into one PR when review capacity (not implementation time) is the bottleneck — explicit user preference established mid-session to reduce CodeRabbit review-slot consumption.

When an agent's follow-up issue reveals its fix converts a latent/silent bug into a live, reachable one (e.g. #1208 making retry-forever paths reachable), that follow-up should be folded into the current PR rather than deferred.

Always verify GitHub event ordering via the Timeline API (`issues/{n}/timeline`) rather than trusting an agent's self-reported sequence of events when diagnosing causality (e.g. rate-limit attribution).

A CI gate that silently skips (Contract Suite skips when CONTRACT_API_URL unset) can make `cargo test --workspace` report success while covering zero of that suite — always confirm a suite actually ran against a live stack when its coverage matters.

Post a disposition comment (per-item: taken / already-true / rejected-with-reason / deferred-to-issue) after every /resolve-pr-reviews pass covering both inline threads AND nitpicks — nitpicks create no threads so the standard flow can silently skip them; this rule was missing from the actual command file and had to be added.

When rewriting a git commit message to avoid a closing-keyword auto-closing an issue prematurely, the PR BODY alone is insufficient — a squash-merge concatenates commit messages too, so the commit message itself must be rewritten (with `git commit --amend`/rebase, verifying `git diff` is empty).

friction: Repeated exit-code masking bugs: piping cargo/clippy/markdownlint through `tail`/`tee` in zsh silently reports the pipe's exit code instead of the actual tool's, causing multiple false-green reports across the session.

GitHub API (`api.github.com`) intermittently refused connections throughout the session (`connection refused`), requiring retry loops everywhere; discovered later this was a host-level network block distinct from git-over-HTTPS which worked fine.

Own review-cycle automation script (`recycle-*.sh`) had multiple serious bugs discovered only in production: CI-pending-check filter never matched running checks (MINCHECKS was the only real gate), clean-verdict detection required non-empty review body (missing the actual empty-body-on-head clean signal), re-drafting on a failed poll actively burned review slots at merge time, and a cadence 'failed open' collapsing a 62-minute wait to 60 seconds on an unreadable clock.
Live-edited a running shell script mid-execution, corrupting the running process (bash reads scripts incrementally by byte offset).
Subagent-filed GitHub issues repeatedly (7+ times) arrived with only the `v2-build` label — no milestone, component label, or parent — requiring manual hygiene fixes each time.
Local API processes from earlier sessions stayed running on ports 3000/3100 with stale env vars, causing 5 phantom test failures that looked like real regressions.

Confirmed the 'remote environment' probed via Agent tool was not actually a separate cloud environment — it ran on the same local Mac, so handoff to an offline-resilient environment required manually packaging shell scripts for the user to run in claude.ai/code instead.
Docker Desktop wedged from filling its VM disk (build cache + dangling images), requiring force-kill and ~23GB of pruning to recover.
open_items: #1220: partial-outage vault-provisioning vacancy-probe gap not closed (a down endpoint + a live endpoint both answering plausibly could still allow a double-mint); superseded in principle by ADR 0007 (derived/idempotent genesis seeds) which remains status=Proposed, undecided by user.
#1221/#1222 (orphaned-root reclaim, concurrent-provision fork adoption) deferred as 'PR D', gated on ADR 0007 acceptance and on #1219 merging.
#1240: CreateInviteLink has no facade mint path — needs a grant-row publish into scope commitment plus a fragment surface; #1165 stays open blocked on it.
#1244: mint a read-scoped accelerator token instead of presenting the full session JWT to the gateway (currently full JWT bound only by TLS-or-loopback check).
#1245: dead acceleratorBearer WASM parameter cannot be safely removed without a hand-written TS interface (EngineWasm) silently misaligning fields — needs a generated-bindings typecheck first.

#1247: saving a downloaded file writes the wrong bytes (SPA fallback index.html) with no error surfaced — reproduced only inside Playwright, unresolved whether it's a real product bug or a harness (CDP download capture) artifact; user was mid-UAT verifying this via a documented manual protocol when session ended.
#1248: a second forced ManualRefresh while one is in flight displaces it and neither drains.
#1249: apps/web's engineHostConfig never sets `profile`, so CI/dev bundles run the 30s production poll cadence instead of a fast CI profile.
#1250: mock-ipns-routing docker image is broken/stale; needs Dockerfile fix (pnpm vs npm) and image rebuild.

#1253: wallet/email login regression — ADR 0008 drafted (cbn#64) and blueprint edits (api.md, web-client.md, desktop.md) pushed but not yet reviewed/merged; will require several linked implementation issues (custom Web3Auth verifier restoration, shared host-agnostic orchestration package, per-host credential-collection seams) not yet filed.

#1254 (Google client-ID conflation, coreKit.ts using one clientId for both Web3Auth project ID and Google OAuth client ID) closed as not-planned, folded into #1253 — staging's VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var likely also broken the same way (unverified in staging).

AGENTS.md rule 4 (all crypto in crates/core) needs an explicit carve-out sentence for browser-held non-extractable WebCrypto key custody (per #1175's implementation in PR #1242) — user had not yet ruled on this at last mention.
#1233 status: settings_record.rs ephemeral-reuse doc line was fixed in PR #1234, but this was flagged as scope-limited (only touched lines in scope of that PR).

Wave 9 review queue (#1246, #1241, #1242, #1243) was mid-flight via handed-off shell scripts on a remote/other Claude Code instance when the session's local machine went offline; user confirmed all merged upon return but rule-4 policy question and review order were answered implicitly via the handoff rather than explicit sign-off captured in this transcript.
